items.title: Anthropic completes $119.5B total IPO and placement financing as shares retreat toward issue price
items.summary: Anthropic confirmed the full exercise of its IPO underwriters' option and closing of a $26 billion strategic private placement, taking aggregate gross proceeds including selling stockholder shares to about $119.5 billion. Shares fell sharply toward the $83 IPO price in Friday premarket trading. Liquidity improves, but profitability, massive compute commitments and concentrated supplier financing remain uncertain.

observations.label: November 20 pre-opening observation; Business Insider and Financial Times
observations.value: ANT approximately $84.84, down about 12.5% versus November 19 closing $97.17; FT reports as much as 13% lower premarket; not confirmed closing performance

observations.label: November 20 confirmed IPO closing; company announcement and Reuters
observations.value: 1,127,000,000 Class A shares at $83; gross offering $93.5B, including fully exercised 147M-share option and secondary proceeds; company receives ~$91.6B of offering gross

observations.label: November 20 completed private placement; Anthropic
observations.value: $26.0B Class N shares subscribed by AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners; total aggregate gross offering plus placement ~$119.5B including selling shareholders' shares

observations.label: Fundamentals, risks and invalidation
observations.value: Liquidity improves but computing commitments, dilution, supplier financing concentration and operating losses persist; watch ANT near $83 issue price, revenue and margins, AI sector breadth and financing rates; better cash generation or demand confirmation weakens downside thesis

items.key_finding: Record AI financing closed, but substantial premarket reversal underscores the gap between capital raised and proven cash economics.

items.title: Bloom Energy tumbles again despite strong growth and analyst upgrade
items.summary: Bloom Energy slid further in Friday premarket trading, leaving shares over 50 percent below their June high, while BMO upgraded the stock to Outperform. October quarterly revenue grew 138 percent and management raised guidance. Negative quarterly free cash flow, customer concentration and data-center construction execution make valuation recovery uncertain.

observations.label: November 20 premarket quote, Barron's
observations.value: BE approximately -7.3%, a non-closing premarket indication; more than 51% below June high, despite positive calendar-year performance

observations.label: November 19 BMO analyst assessment, multiple sources
observations.value: Upgrade to Outperform from Market Perform with target cut to $230 from $260; cites improved project execution but cost competitiveness and customer concentration remain risks

observations.label: October 22 company Q3 2026 results
observations.value: Revenue $1,235.8M, up 138.1% year on year; GAAP operating income $225.4M; FY26 revenue guidance $4.4B to $4.6B

observations.label: Cash flow and next indicators
observations.value: Q3 free cash flow around negative $181M and operating cash flow about negative $27M; monitor fourth-quarter billing, contract assets, cash conversion, Oracle/Nebius installations, and data-center build schedules; repeated cash burn or deployments delays weaken case

items.key_finding: Bloom shows strong revenue and operating growth but material valuation reset amid cash conversion and execution risk.

items.title: Saudi coalition reports fresh Houthi drone and missile interceptions as port threats rise
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Friday morning it intercepted five drones and one ballistic missile, with Riyadh among reported targets. AP reports the count and Reuters separately confirms the missile interception and southern drone alerts. Threats involving ports raise Red Sea logistics risk, but there is no verified new Saudi oil-production shutdown or sustained export loss.

observations.label: November 20 morning official report carried by AP
observations.value: Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting five drones and one ballistic missile; Riyadh reportedly among targets; count sourced to coalition, not independently verified

observations.label: Reuters November 20 independent reporting
observations.value: Reported ballistic missile interception toward southern Saudi Arabia and drone alerts for Jazan, Abha and Khamis Mushait

observations.label: Oil-market cross-check, 6:55 AM EST November 20
observations.value: January Brent about $91.42 (-0.61%) and January WTI about $82.23 (-0.25%), indicative market quotes; no newly established sustained export volume loss

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: Threats to ports and Red Sea maritime routes could raise freight or insurance cost; monitor Saudi Aramco operations, Yanbu pipeline, Bab el-Mandeb transits, UKMTO/MARAD, tanker loadings and export volumes; uninterrupted flows or de-escalation weaken supply-risk thesis

items.key_finding: Newly reported Saudi interceptions elevate maritime-security risk without verified incremental oil-flow loss.

items.title: California attorney general subpoenas Nvidia amid China chip and disclosure inquiry
items.summary: California's attorney general issued an investigative subpoena to Nvidia regarding whether advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether investors were misled. The inquiry is confirmed, but wrongdoing has not been established. Nvidia shares declined in early premarket trading, adding legal uncertainty despite recent strong revenue growth.

observations.label: November 20 premarket indicative quote
observations.value: NVDA approximately $142.35, -2.49% versus prior close; time of individual quote not specified by quote provider; not a confirmed close

observations.label: November 19 official legal catalyst
observations.value: California DOJ investigative subpoena concerning possible transfer of advanced chips/confidential information to China and investor statements; no finding of violation

observations.label: Assessment, risks and invalidation
observations.value: Strong chip revenue versus governance, export compliance and legal costs; monitor Nvidia disclosures, California DOJ actions, congressional testimony and customer orders; exculpatory findings weaken legal risk

items.key_finding: Verified subpoena introduces compliance uncertainty, not proof of export violations or demand collapse.

sources.title: California DOJ official November 19 subpoena announcement

items.title: Intuit cuts fiscal 2027 revenue outlook and agrees to sell Mailchimp
items.summary: Intuit lowered its annual revenue outlook because of weaker Credit Karma expectations despite solid quarterly profit growth. The company also agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons. Shares dropped sharply in premarket indications, making this a material software-growth versus valuation watch; transaction closing and future guidance remain uncertain.

observations.label: November 20 5:09 AM EST premarket report
observations.value: INTU approximately $274.52, -11.4% indicated; premarket not closing move

observations.label: Intuit official November 19 Q1 FY27 earnings
observations.value: Revenue $4.4B, +12% YoY; online ecosystem revenue +20%; adjusted EPS $2.91

observations.label: FY27 guidance and divestiture
observations.value: Revenue $23.081B-$23.365B; Mailchimp sale ~$3.68B ($3.31B cash and $368M Bending Spoons shares), planned early-2027 close

observations.label: Risks and next checks
observations.value: Credit Karma business trajectory, organic software growth, customer retention, profitability and deal approvals; improved guidance and conversion would weaken selloff rationale

items.key_finding: Intuit's guidance reduction drove sharp premarket weakness despite operating growth and a major planned divestiture.
